<p class="cycle-role">Choices about which uncertainties and evidence gaps merit investigation.</p>

<p class="page-deck"><strong>Which new evidence would most improve urban climate decisions?</strong></p>

Once the limits of existing evidence become visible, a further question follows: which additional evidence would materially improve decisions? The absence of a study does not, by itself, establish a research priority. Some gaps may have little consequence, while a carefully chosen new case, evaluation, dataset or causal test may resolve uncertainty for many cities.

This theme examines where new evidence could alter an appraisal, clarify an important mechanism, correct systematic exclusion or expand the range of cities able to learn. It connects evidence mapping with choices about research design, asking not only where knowledge is missing, but where producing new knowledge could make a consequential difference.

::: {.notice}
**Analytical boundary.** This theme concerns prospective choices about what evidence should be produced next. A data gap, new tool or under-studied location is not automatically a research priority.

**Place in the learning cycle.** New evidence matters most when it changes what decision-makers understand about how climate action can be delivered or what it may cause.
:::

## Questions the lab investigates

- Which unresolved questions could materially alter an urban climate decision?
- Where could a new case, evaluation or dataset clarify an important mechanism?
- Which systematic exclusions limit the learning options available to multiple cities?

## Connections across the learning cycle

- **Input from [Geographies of Climate Learning](/research/geographies-of-climate-learning.html):** Mapping the reach and limits of existing knowledge reveals which unresolved questions could be consequential enough to justify new research.
- **Next stage — [Modes of Climate Delivery](/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html):** New evidence matters most when it changes what decision-makers understand about how climate action can be delivered or what it may cause.
- **Return loop:** Consequences generate new evidence, reveal unresolved questions and revise what other cities may plausibly learn.
